newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens firmer in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens firmer in light trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened a touch stronger at C$1.3754 (US$0.7270) in light trading on Tuesday after another quiet night on overseas markets, dealers said. * They said there was likely to be more interest in the unit than yesterday when market holidays in the United States and Great Britain threw a blanket over currency trading.
The United States will hold its US$15 billion auction of three- and six-month T-bills at 1330 EDT/1730 GMT.
"There is a fair bit of new supply coming on stream, so that will be watched to see how the market responds," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser with CIBC Wood Gundy.
With little in the way of new economic data this week, markets were expected to refocus attention on the winding down of Canada's June 2 general election campaign.
A Reuters-Zogby poll released yesterday showed the governing Liberals with a commanding lead over all rivals.
At the same time, support for the Quebec separatist Bloc Quebecois seemed to have trailed off, the poll suggested.
"Bad news for the Bloc should translate into a firmer Canadian dollar, and the market will watch very closely how Quebec votes," Farrill said.
But other traders speculated that the election could be much closer than the polls have indicated, with a possibility that the Western-based Reform Party will form the official opposition.
That scenario could keep the emotional national unity issue on the front burner and place pressure on the dollar.

"Over the long term, that would be negative for the currency because we will be going into more discussion of the sovereignty issue later this year," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed-income analyst with MMS International.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 84.48 yen from Monday's close of 83.96 and jumped to 1.2321 marks from Monday's 1.2307 marks.
